transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Hi, Doctor. Um… I guess what brings me in is I haven’t really been wanting to do the things that usually keep me going. Salsa nights, church gatherings, cooking for the neighbors… even just walking into my shop to enjoy the smell of the wood. I know that may sound small, but it’s not really like me.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, lately?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but most mornings I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. It’s like the color’s gone out of the house, if that makes sense. I try to keep myself together, especially in front of my wife, but some days I really have to force it.
Have you found that you don’t take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like salsa nights or cooking for your neighbors?

Yes… I have. I mean, I’m trying not to be dramatic about it, but that’s really what scared me enough to come in. Salsa nights used to lift me up, church gatherings too, and I liked cooking for the neighbors. Even just going into my shop and smelling the wood used to make me feel like myself. Lately I just… don’t want to do any of it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling unusually tired or lacking energy, even when you haven’t done much physically?

Yeah… I have. I don’t want to sound lazy, because I’m not usually like that, but even if I’ve been sitting most of the day, or I’ve had a full night in bed, my body still feels worn out. Like I’ve been framing a roof all day.

Little things, like loading tools into the truck, feel like more than they should. I keep thinking I ought to just push through it, but it’s been hard. Is that what you mean?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately, like not wanting to eat as much or losing weight without trying?

I’m not really sure, to be honest. I haven’t been keeping track of my weight or anything. My wife might notice before I do.

I guess my appetite hasn’t been something I’ve paid much attention to… some meals I eat because it’s time to eat, not because I’m excited about it. But I don’t know if I’ve lost weight. I don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure. Does that answer it okay?
Have you noticed yourself eating more or less than usual, or have you lost or gained weight recently without trying?

I don’t think I can say for sure. I haven’t weighed myself lately, and I haven’t really been paying close attention to portions or anything.

Maybe I’m eating a little more out of habit some days, or less on others, but nothing I could confidently say is a real change. I don’t want to overstate it if it’s not there. Is that okay?
Have you noticed any unintentional weight loss or gain lately, even if you haven’t been trying to change your weight?

I honestly haven’t noticed anything clear like that. I don’t really weigh myself, and my clothes don’t seem dramatically different or anything.

So… I don’t think I’ve had a big gain or loss, at least not that I can tell. Sorry, I know that’s not a very exact answer.
Would you say that your lack of interest in activities, like salsa nights or going into your shop, has been a significant change from how you usually are?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but that’s really what brought me in.

Those are usually the things that keep me steady—salsa nights, church gatherings, cooking something for the neighbors, even just walking into my shop because I like the smell of the wood. Lately I just… don’t want to do them. I know that’s not like me.

Is that the kind of change you mean?
Would you say that this heavy, empty feeling in your chest and lack of interest in doing things has been happening most days for at least 2 weeks now?

Yes… it’s definitely been more than two weeks.

I kept telling myself it was just a rough patch, maybe stress or me being tired, but if I’m being honest, it’s been dragging on for about six months now. Not every single minute, but most days it’s there enough that it doesn’t feel like just a bad week anymore.

That’s… that’s the right way to answer that, I think?
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or feeling restless and unable to sit still?

Yeah… a bit. I mean, I didn’t really notice it at first, or maybe I didn’t want to.

Some of the guys at the job have mentioned I’m moving really slow lately—like I’m taking forever just to pick up a board or get started on something. One of them joked it was like my boots were full of wet cement.

And then other times I’m kind of the opposite… pacing around the shop, rubbing my hands, looking busy but not actually getting anything useful done. It’s embarrassing to say, but yes, I guess that’s been happening. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you had any thoughts of not wanting to live anymore or that life isn’t worth living?

I… I don’t want to alarm anybody. I’m not trying to be dramatic.

But yes, I have had thoughts like… maybe it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And sometimes I catch myself thinking my family might be better off without me, which scares me as soon as I think it.

I’m sorry, that’s hard to say out loud. Is that what you mean?
